provenance.paper_title: MementoGUI: Learning Agentic Multimodal Memory Control for Long-Horizon GUI Agents

representation_paths.memory_component: localized visual references for task-relevant interface events

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: Working-memory events retain ROI-level visual evidence alongside concise summaries for later GUI decisions.

representation_paths.memory_component: event summaries and retrieved past trajectories

evidence.paraphrase: MementoCore performs step processing, compression, episodic writing, and learned episodic selection over reusable trajectories.

A trained controller selects online memory events and executes specialized working- and episodic-memory operators. For MementoGUI, this specifically supports a trained but frozen update module of localized visual references for task-relevant interface events.

Selected interaction history is compressed into concise event summaries while preserving localized visual cues. For MementoGUI, this specifically supports episodic or hierarchical summarization of localized visual references for task-relevant interface events.

derived.hybrid_relation: Text summaries and ROI-level screenshots are jointly preserved as structured multimodal events.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 4): Training learns the gate and consolidation module. Deployment uses those frozen modules to update memory state, which is T2, not policy evolution. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
